title: Be an island
hookLine: to Ananda: be islands to yourselves, a refuge to yourselves, the dhamma your refuge (DN 16)

lines: NOT THE ANSWER HE HOPED FOR.
cards: A waiting room, a phone that won't ring, and one question underneath everything: what happens to us without them? Ananda sits in the shade beside the Buddha, who has just come through a serious illness.

Ananda has been his attendant for many years. While the teacher lay sick, he admits, he held on to one comfort: surely the teacher would not pass away without leaving some last instruction for the community. Some plan.
Someone in charge. The Buddha's answer isn't the one Ananda was hoping for. It hands the question straight back to him.

teach.h: NO CLOSED FIST, NOTHING HELD BACK.
teach.b: First, the Buddha says, what does the community expect of me? I've taught everything, with nothing held back. There's no closed fist of a teacher here, no secret saved for the favorites.
And I've never thought of myself as the one who must lead the community. So why would I leave a leader? Then comes the line.

teach.h: DIPA: AN ISLAND, OR A LAMP.
teach.b: The key Pali word is dipa, and it has two meanings: an island, and a lamp. Translators have gone both ways. In 1881 T.
W. Rhys Davids rendered it with lamps: "be ye lamps unto yourselves. Be ye a refuge to yourselves."
Other translators hear island: be an island to yourself, a refuge to yourself, with the dhamma as your island, the dhamma as your refuge, and no other.

teach.h: THE ISLAND IS BUILT BY PRACTICE.
teach.b: An island is solid ground when the flood is rising all around. A lamp is light when everyone else's has gone out. Either way, the point is the same.
Don't lean your whole weight on a person, even me. Stand on what you've seen for yourself, and on the teaching itself. How?

The Buddha answers right there: by practicing mindfulness, watching the body, feelings, the mind and the way things are, steadily, with clear attention. The island isn't stubbornness, and it isn't going it alone.
It's having practiced enough that when the waters rise, there's ground under your feet. A teacher who refuses to name a successor tells his students to be their own light, and their own ground.

how: Buddhist teachers often quote 'be an island to yourself' (or 'be a lamp') to encourage self-reliance grounded in practice, and the four foundations of mindfulness that the Buddha names here are still taught as a meditation practice.

o: a refuge hall where monks gather to chant
an island, and also a lamp: one Pali word
a raft for crossing to the far shore

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: the Buddha named a successor to lead the community
he said he'd never thought of himself as its leader, and told them to be their own island.
the Pali word dipa can mean both island and lamp
the Buddha kept secret teachings for his closest students
he said there was no closed fist of a teacher: nothing held back.

games.q: you're the Buddha. Ananda is frightened and hopes you'll leave instructions and someone in charge. what do you tell him?
o: name your most trusted disciple as leader.
tell him to be an island to himself, with the dhamma as refuge.
promise to stay until he's ready.
games.why: no successor. be an island, a refuge to yourselves, the dhamma your refuge, and build that island by practicing mindfulness.

practice: Feel the ground under you, the chair, the floor, the steadiness of it: that's your island for now.

Think of one small decision you've been waiting for someone else to make, what to eat, whether to call, which way to go, and ask yourself what you actually see and know. Let the answer come from your own ground.

wordCard.voice: Dipa. Island, and also lamp: the Buddha's answer to Ananda, be a dipa and a refuge to yourselves, with the dhamma your refuge.

orig.note: Pali: island, and also lamp. Sanskrit keeps them apart: dvīpa (island), dīpa (lamp).

carryVoice: Your line: be your own island. Or, as Rhys Davids heard it, your own lamp. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: be ye lamps unto yourselves. Be ye a refuge to yourselves.
